unit.why: A quoted note from Hut ha-Meshulash tells how the Hatam Sofer allowed R. Mordechai Banet's body to be reburied in Nikolsburg after Banet appeared to him in a night vision. This is a narrative about non-Hasidic rabbinic figures.
unit.boundary_note: set inside a citation chain: the previous division opens a new quotation (Shoel u-Meshiv) and the next division continues it with a separate tale about kitniyot on Pesach

stories.start_quote: ובחוט המשולש תולדות החת"ם זצ״ל יש
stories.end_quote: לזאת הסכים זקיני ז"ל על הדבר עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: R. Mordechai Banet died in Karlsbad and was buried in Lichtenstadt. Half a year later he appeared to the Hatam Sofer in a night vision and asked to be moved to Nikolsburg, explaining that his temporary burial had been a punishment for breaking off a marriage match in his youth. The Hatam Sofer then permitted the reburial.

tags.why: Praises the non-Hasidic sages Banet and the Hatam Sofer; the story is copied from Hut ha-Meshulash
